name: Rekt News
machineReadable: RSS https://rekt.news/rss/feed.xml (works); leaderboard JSON embedded in __NEXT_DATA__ at https://rekt.news/leaderboard/ (328 entries: title, rekt.amount, rekt.date, audit, tags)
coverage: 2020 onward (leaderboard includes retro entries for 2020 LuBian etc.); ~328 ranked write-ups
metadata: Date, USD amount, audit status, tags, long-form narrative; no structured tx hashes or root-cause field
updateFrequency: Irregular; RSS lastBuildDate 2026-10-16 but newest item dated 2026-04-09, newer posts appear to be editorial
concerns: Editorial/satirical tone, only notable hacks, root cause buried in prose; posting cadence has slowed in 2026.
notes: Good canonical narrative links; Oak Security's dataset is built on this archive.

name: Rekt Hub Leaderboard
machineReadable: JSON API https://hub.rekt.news/api/leaderboard (confirmed, 321 rows: id, slug, title, rektAmount, rektDate, rektAudit); also /api/feed?limit=100, /api/content
metadata: Title, slug, USD amount, date (M/D/YYYY strings), audit status
concerns: Vite SPA, undocumented API; inconsistent date formats; duplicates rekt.news entirely.
notes: Easiest machine-readable path to rekt.news amounts; use slug to link https://rekt.news/<slug>.

name: DefiLlama Hacks
machineReadable: https://api.llama.fi/hacks (confirmed, 1306 records, JSON array)
chains: All major chains incl. Bitcoin, CEX hacks; chain is an array field
metadata: date (unix), name, classification, technique, amount, chain[], bridgeHack, targetType, returnedFunds, defillamaId, language; source field is empty in all rows; no tx hashes
license: DefiLlama data is open/free to use (open-source project); no explicit license on endpoint
concerns: Web page returns 403 to curl (Cloudflare) but API is open; no source URLs or tx hashes; amounts are USD at time of hack.
notes: Best structured backbone: two-level root-cause taxonomy (classification+technique) and widest time range.

name: SlowMist Hacked
machineReadable: none (server-rendered HTML; scrape https://hacked.slowmist.io/en/?c=&page=N, ~116 pages; filters ?c=<category>&d=<year>)
chains: ETH, BSC, Tron, EOS, Polygon, HECO, Fantom, Solana, Avalanche, Polkadot, Arbitrum, Optimism, zkSync, Base, plus Exchange/Wallet/Bridge/NFT/Blockchain categories
metadata: Date, target, description, loss amount, attack method, reference source links; no tx hashes
concerns: No API; attack-method labels are coarse and free-text; includes scams/phishing.
notes: Includes L1/consensus incidents (e.g. Pirate Chain transaction validation bug Oct 2026); strong Asian-ecosystem coverage.

name: DeFiHackLabs Explorer
machineReadable: https://defihacklabs.io/explorer/incidents.json (917 rows: date, name, type, Lost, lossType, Contract, chain) and https://defihacklabs.io/explorer/rootcause_data.json (754 keyed entries with type, date, rootCause narrative); both confirmed
chains: EVM chains (Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum, Base, Polygon, etc.) plus some Solana
metadata: Date, name, attack type, loss, chain, contract; root-cause narrative per incident
updateFrequency: Explorer JSON versioned 2026-06-18 / last entry 2026-08-09; lags the GitHub repo
concerns: Explorer snapshot lags the repo by ~2 months; loss units mix USD and tokens (lossType).
notes: Friendly JSON front-end of the DeFiHackLabs repo (#22).

name: BlockSec Security Incidents
machineReadable: POST https://blocksec.com/api/v1/attack/events with JSON body {} (confirmed, returns all 308: id, project, loss, chainIds, transactions[txnHash, attacker, chainId], rootCause, date, poc, rescued); GET https://blocksec.com/api/v1/attack/events-root-cause
chains: EVM by chainId (Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Polygon, Avalanche, Berachain, etc.)
metadata: Date, loss, chain IDs, attack tx hashes, attacker address, root-cause label, PoC link (96/308), rescued amount
concerns: Undocumented API (GET returns 403); EVM-only and from 2023 only.
notes: Best structured tx-hash + attacker + root-cause source; links into Phalcon explorer traces.

name: RevertIQ Hacks
machineReadable: https://revertiqapi.azurewebsites.net/hacks?page=1 (returns all 1430 items, ~12MB); /hacks/summary; /hacks/catalog?page=1&pageSize=N; /hacks/<slug> (all confirmed)
chains: 144 chains incl. Bitcoin, Cosmos, Solana, Starknet, TON, Sui, XRPL
metadata: incident_date, amount_lost_usd, chains, attack_vectors, root_cause text, markdown description, source_names/links, tags, protocol_types
concerns: AI-generated summaries; many entries cite DefiLlama as source, so heavy duplication; SPA with undocumented API.
notes: Richest per-incident text with multi-source citations; useful for enrichment and dedup cross-checks.

name: ChainSec DeFi Hacks
machineReadable: none (server-rendered Next.js HTML)
metadata: Date, project, short description, USD amount, one news source link
concerns: Small, news-sourced, no root cause or tx data; stopped updating in April 2026.
notes: Subset of DefiLlama/rekt; low incremental value.

name: Smart Contracts Hacking - Web3 Hacks Dashboard
machineReadable: none (HTML with data-date/data-amount/data-chain/data-technique attributes, 30 rows per page; scrapable)
metadata: Name, date, amount, chain, technique
concerns: Technique labels are concatenated duplicates (e.g. 'Acces Control Exploit / Improper Access Control'), suggesting a merge of DefiLlama and others without dedup; reCAPTCHA on site.
notes: Aggregator; use only to find gaps, not as primary data.

name: Cryptomortem
machineReadable: none
metadata: Unknown
concerns: Cloudflare error 521 (origin server down); no Wayback snapshots.
notes: Broken link; drop or recheck later.

name: Web3 Is Going Just Great
machineReadable: Atom feed https://www.web3isgoinggreat.com/feed.xml (confirmed); first entries in __NEXT_DATA__ (fields: date, title, body, filters.blockchain/tech/theme, readableId); backend is Firebase RTDB
metadata: Date, title, HTML body, blockchain/tech/theme tags, collections (e.g. bridge-attack, flash-loan-attack), sometimes amounts
license: Content copyright Molly White; code on GitHub (molly/web3-is-going-just-great)
concerns: Covers scams, rugs, collapses and commentary, not only hacks; no structured amount or root-cause fields.
notes: Good for context and non-technical incidents; filter by theme=hack.

name: Blockchain Graveyard
machineReadable: Jekyll _posts markdown in gh-pages branch of github.com/magoo/Blockchain-Graveyard; feed.xml (link in page is malformed)
chains: Bitcoin/altcoin exchanges and custodians, some ETH
metadata: Name, date, estimated root cause (social engineering, cloud takeover, app vuln), narrative and source links
concerns: Stale and small; root causes are estimates.
notes: Useful only for early (2011-2016) CEX breaches with root-cause guesses.

name: De.Fi Rekt Database
machineReadable: GraphQL https://public-api.de.fi/graphql (query 'rekts'; returns 'Missing API key' without key); docs as markdown https://docs.de.fi/audits/rekt-database.md
coverage: Docs page only; underlying DB at https://de.fi/rekt-database spans ~2011 onward (thousands of entries incl. rugs/scams)
metadata: Project, date, funds lost/returned, chain, category, type (exploit/rug/etc.), auditor, affected addresses, description
concerns: The URL is documentation, not the data; mixes rugs and exit scams with hacks.
notes: Unique 'auditor' field is valuable for audit-vs-exploit analysis; request API key.

name: SEAL 911 Activity Log
machineReadable: Raw markdown https://raw.githubusercontent.com/security-alliance/seal-911/main/ACTIVITY.md (88 bullet entries)
metadata: Incident name and one link (tweet/postmortem); no dates or amounts
concerns: Incomplete by design; links mostly to X posts; no structured fields.
notes: Useful for whitehat-rescue and near-miss incidents (e.g. Geth DoS, Aptos struct hijack).

name: DeFiHacks Wiki
machineReadable: none
metadata: Unknown (wiki pages)
concerns: Domain returns NXDOMAIN (expired); only archive.org copies remain.
notes: Broken link; use http://web.archive.org/web/2022/https://defihacks.wiki/ if needed.

name: Cyfrin Solodit
machineReadable: POST https://solodit.cyfrin.io/api/v1/solodit/findings (requires X-Cyfrin-API-Key; returns 401 'Missing API key' without)
coverage: ~2021 onward; tens of thousands of audit and contest findings
chains: EVM mostly, plus Solana, Move, Cosmos, etc.
metadata: Title, impact/severity, firm/source, protocol, category tags, finders, quality/rarity, report link
license: Free account; terms of service apply to findings
concerns: Audit findings, not incidents; needs free API key and rate limits.
notes: Best source to map exploit root causes to prior audit findings.

name: Smart Contract VulnDB (tintinweb)
machineReadable: https://tintinweb.github.io/smart-contract-vulndb/cache/vulns-1.json and vulns-2.json (confirmed; JSON-lines, 25k issues per file)
coverage: Audit reports up to early 2024; ~40k+ issues
metadata: title, severity, markdown body, dataSource (name, repo, url)
concerns: Not updated since 2024; no taxonomy labels; files are JSONL not JSON.
notes: Bulk audit-finding text for NLP classification.

name: CVE Smart Contracts (SmartBugs)
machineReadable: Raw files: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smartbugs/CVE-Smart-Contracts/main/cve.json, data/index.csv, metadata.json
coverage: CVE snapshot 2026-07-24; ~542 contracts (2018-era token CVEs mostly)
metadata: CVE ID, address, source, bytecode, CWE/SWC/Iuliano-DiNucci labels, function-level locations
concerns: Mostly old integer-overflow ERC20 CVEs; claims not independently verified.
notes: High-quality labels but narrow scope; good for taxonomy mapping.

name: FORGE Artifacts
machineReadable: Git repo: dataset/results/*.json (6,454 audit-report JSONs), dataset-curated/; see also github.com/shenyimings/FORGE-Curated
coverage: Audit reports through ~2024, curated set Dec 2024-Feb 2026; 27,497 vulnerabilities
metadata: Per-report findings with CWE classification, severity, location, linked source files
concerns: LLM-extracted and LLM-classified (CWE), so label noise; audit findings, not exploits.
notes: Largest CWE-labelled finding set (ICSE'26); good for training a root-cause classifier.

name: Immunefi Web3 Security Library
machineReadable: none (markdown link lists; raw via raw.githubusercontent.com)
metadata: Links grouped as Bug Fix Reviews, Hack Analyses, Vulnerabilities, Tools
concerns: Link list only, no data fields; link rot likely.
notes: Use HackAnalyses/BugFixReviews as postmortem URL seeds.

name: SCV-List
machineReadable: Raw markdown table https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sirhashalot/SCV-List/main/README.md (~160 rows)
metadata: Protocol, date, finder, bounty, writeup link
concerns: Stale; deliberately excludes hacks with losses.
notes: Only source focused on disclosed-but-not-exploited mainnet bugs.

name: DeFiHackLabs (GitHub)
machineReadable: Git repo: src/test/YYYY-MM/<Name>_exp.sol (886 Foundry PoCs); README.md incident list (raw.githubusercontent.com); add_new_entry.py
chains: EVM (Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum, Base, Polygon, Optimism, etc.)
metadata: Date, name, root-cause description, lost amount, attacker/contract addresses, attack tx links, runnable Foundry PoC
updateFrequency: Several commits per week; last commit 2026-10-16
concerns: EVM-only; README is markdown not structured; focuses on reproducible small/medium DeFi exploits.
notes: Gold standard for technical root cause + tx + reproducible PoC.

name: Bitcoin Core Security Advisories
machineReadable: RSS https://bitcoincore.org/en/rss.xml and https://bitcoincore.org/en/feed.xml (confirmed 200); per-advisory pages /en/YYYY/MM/DD/disclose-cve-*/
metadata: CVE, severity (low/medium/high/critical), affected/fixed versions, disclosure date, description
concerns: No JSON API; node-level bugs, rarely tied to loss amounts.
notes: Primary source for consensus/node bugs (inflation bug CVE-2018-17144, DoS, crashes).

name: Geth Vulnerability Disclosures
machineReadable: https://geth.ethereum.org/docs/vulnerabilities/vulnerabilities.json (confirmed, 12 entries) + .minisig signature; GitHub advisories for ethereum/go-ethereum
metadata: name, uid (GETH-YYYY-NN), summary, description, links, introduced, fixed, published, severity, check regex, CVE
concerns: Small list; other clients (Nethermind, Besu, Prysm, Lighthouse) not covered.
notes: Clean signed JSON for node DoS/consensus bugs; good template for infra-bug schema.

name: Cosmos Security Advisories (ASA)
machineReadable: Raw markdown table https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cosmos/security/main/ADVISORIES.md (links to GHSA IDs)
metadata: ASA ID, team, severity, title, GHSA link
concerns: Short table; details live in GHSA pages.
notes: Many entries are chain-halt bugs (CometBFT, IBC-Go non-determinism).

name: Cosmos SDK GitHub Security Advisories
machineReadable: OSV API POST https://api.osv.dev/v1/query {package:{name:'github.com/cosmos/cosmos-sdk',ecosystem:'Go'}} (confirmed, 24 vulns); GitHub REST /repos/cosmos/cosmos-sdk/security-advisories
metadata: GHSA/CVE/GO IDs, severity, CVSS, affected/patched versions, description, references
concerns: GitHub HTML/API blocked from this sandbox (403), verified via OSV instead.
notes: Use OSV for all Go/Rust chain repos (cometbft, ibc-go, go-ethereum, solana, sui, aptos).

name: GitHub Advisory Database
machineReadable: https://api.github.com/advisories (REST, token recommended); git repo github.com/github/advisory-database (OSV JSON, ls-remote confirmed); also https://api.osv.dev
chains: Any chain whose clients/libs are in npm, Go, crates, PyPI, Maven
metadata: GHSA ID, CVE, CWE, severity/CVSS, affected ranges, references
concerns: Web and API returned 403 from this sandbox (proxy policy), so not tested directly; very broad, needs keyword/package filtering.
notes: Best bulk source for blockchain client/library vulns via the advisory-database git repo.

name: NVD Vulnerability Search
machineReadable: https://services.nvd.nist.gov/rest/json/cves/2.0?keywordSearch=smart%20contract (confirmed; 608 results), API key optional for higher rate limits
metadata: CVE ID, CWE, CVSS, CPE, published/modified dates, references
concerns: Search page is a JS SPA; crypto CVEs are noisy (many 2018 ERC20 overflow claims) and need keyword filtering.
notes: Use for CVE cross-reference only.

name: OWASP Smart Contract Top 10
machineReadable: none (MkDocs site; source markdown at github.com/OWASP/owasp-scs)
metadata: SC01-SC10 categories with description, examples, mitigations; Alternate Top 15 Web3 attack vectors
concerns: Taxonomy only, no incident data; category definitions change between editions.
notes: Good public label set for root-cause classification (SC01:2026 Access Control, SC02 Business Logic, etc.).

name: Oak Security Audit Gap Q2 2026
machineReadable: none for article; dashboard at https://research.oaksecurity.io/dashboard/
coverage: 2022 to 2026-06-30; 25,706 audit findings from 22 firms and 237 rekt.news incidents ($8.62B)
metadata: Aggregated statistics by attack vector, quarter, audited vs not
concerns: Analysis, not raw data; incidents derived from rekt.news, so duplicates #1.
notes: Useful methodology for classifying code-vs-operational root causes.
